tests: spawn refuses and creates nothing when the declared shared register cannot be read

consumesExternalOutput.program: tiphys spawn and tiphys teardown, over git ls-remote / git fetch / git cat-file / git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The refusal line embeds git's own stderr through src/exclusion.ts, which spawns git, and SPAWN_GREP matches src/exclusion.ts, src/spawn.ts and src/teardown.ts, so red-witness rule (f) binds this witness. The cited capture is REAL stderr of the shipped `tiphys spawn` and `tiphys teardown`, taken 2026-09-17 on node v26.6.0 with git 2.43.0 against two clones of one fleet home published to a real bare remote. The fixture is the dangerous state itself: environment A acquires the fleet, spawns a scout, and environment B then takes the fleet over with `tiphys lock acquire --take-over`, which advances the register on the remote and cannot touch A's local lease file because `state/` is gitignored and never travels. The named test rebuilds that sequence, substitutes only the four values the capture marks as varying per run (<ENVA>, <ENVB>, <EXPIRES>, <LAB>), and compares the live reason line and exit code byte for byte. The two members are the two ways a fail-closed layer fails open. Member 0 makes an unreachable register classify as `free`, so the guard is asked the right question and gets the answer that licenses the spawn; member 1 leaves the classification correct and drops the refusal at the call site. Falling back to local-only exclusion is the vacuous green this layer exists to prevent (M4-P21 criterion 7), and local-only exclusion is precisely what is already green in this fixture.
